name: IN-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent André Carson running with a large cash advantage
Prediction markets price Carson at 97% to win
Republican challenger has shown no fundraising or polling presence
model.rationale: Indianapolis-based IN-07 leans heavily Democratic, Carson is a well-funded incumbent, and both Kalshi and Polymarket price his win at 97%, matching the fundamentals. No polls or ratings suggest any reason to move off the strong baseline margin of about 25 points.
model.watch: A surprise surge in challenger fundraising or outside spending could narrow the margin, though not enough to threaten the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
André Carson, the longtime Democratic incumbent in this Indianapolis district, is seeking another term against Republican Patrick McAuley and a Libertarian candidate. The district's partisan lean of roughly 21 points Democratic gives Carson a substantial structural advantage, and he has raised over $1 million with more than $600,000 on hand, while his opponent reports no fundraising activity.

Prediction markets on both Kalshi and Polymarket price Carson's win probability at 97 percent, consistent with the fundamentals-based expectation of a margin near 25 points. With no competitive polling, no expert ratings flagging the race, and no signs of challenger resources, this seat is firmly in the Safe D category.
